Low-Downtime Migration: Azure SQL Database to SQL Server (VM) with DACPAC and Change Tracking

Nithin Sunke · November 2, 2026 · 21 min read

Lab 7 of the Azure SQL Database migration series. Labs 5 and 6 copied everything while the application was stopped. This time the 16.7-million-row database is copied while Azure stays live, Change Tracking ships only the rows that changed, and the cutover window shrinks to about a minute and a half, of which the final sync took 3 seconds. Everything is scripted, with no per-table code.

Why not just repeat Lab 6?

In Lab 6 the application had to stay stopped from the first bcp out to the last bcp in. Downtime grows with the size of the database. The only way to shrink it is to do the big copy while the application is still running, and then ship just the rows that changed during and after that copy.

Going from Azure SQL Database back to a VM, most of the usual low-downtime tools are not available:

MethodAzure SQL DB → SQL Server VM?
Log shipping / backup + restoreNo. You can't take native .bak or log backups from Azure SQL Database
Always On availability groupNo. Azure SQL Database can't be the primary
Transactional replication (Lab 4)No. Azure SQL Database can only be a subscriber, never a publisher
Azure DMSNo. It only migrates to a VM from a SQL Server source
SQL Data SyncAvoid. It retires on 30 September 2027 and new customers can't create it
Change Tracking + your own applyYes. A native feature, it works on every tier, including serverless
A DACPAC can't carry deltas. Its data part is always a full snapshot, it inserts only and has no upsert, and it has no idea which rows were deleted. Publishing a second DACPAC with data onto a loaded database just fails on primary keys. DACPAC is the initial load, and Change Tracking does everything after that.

How it works

Azure SQL DB (source)                               SQL Server VM (target)
─────────────────────                               ──────────────────────────────────
CT enabled ── baseline version ──┐
DACPAC extract ──────────────────┼────────────────▶ DACPAC publish (initial load)
                                 │
CHANGETABLE(CHANGES …) ──────────┼─ linked server ─▶ stg.<table> ─▶ MERGE ─▶ <table>
                                 │                   sync.control keeps the watermark
Agent job every 15 minutes ──────┘
Cutover: source READ_ONLY → final sync → validate → finalize target → repoint app

Change Tracking (CT) is lighter than CDC. It doesn't store old or new column values. For every changed row it records only the primary key, the operation (I/U/D) and a version number:

  • Every committed transaction moves a database-wide version forward, which CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION() returns.
  • CHANGETABLE(CHANGES t, @last) returns the net change per row since @last. Ten updates to one row come back as one row.
  • Joining back to the base table gives the current values. If the join finds nothing, the row was deleted.
  • History is kept for CHANGE_RETENTION days. If your watermark is older than CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION(), or someone ran TRUNCATE, the delta is no longer trustworthy and the table must be reloaded.

For an Oracle DBA, it's close to a materialized view log with a fast refresh driven by a primary key: the log knows which keys changed, and the refresh reads the current row.

The ordering that makes it safe

  1. Enable CT on the source.
  2. Record the CT version: the baseline.
  3. Only then extract the DACPAC with data.

An extract from a live database isn't a point-in-time copy. Some rows may change while the extract runs. Because the baseline was taken before the extract, those rows show up again in the first delta, and the MERGE reapplies the latest state. Overlap is harmless. A gap would lose data, which is why the order matters.

Lab environment and the toolkit

ComponentThis lab
Sourcecisql01.database.windows.net / scsbank, General Purpose serverless GP_S_Gen5_1, 2.3 GB
TargetSQL Server 2025 (17.0.1000.7) Enterprise Developer on MSSQLSRV01, database scsbank
Linked server providerMSOLEDBSQL (OLE DB Driver 18; MSOLEDBSQL19 is also installed)
ToolsSqlPackage, sqlcmd (ODBC 18), PowerShell, SQL Agent
Data17 tables in 9 schemas, 16,760,354 rows, all tables have a primary key, 25 foreign keys

Writing a staging table and a MERGE by hand for every table works for five tables, but not for fifty. So the whole method is packaged as a small toolkit: one generic engine that builds every statement at run time from metadata, and one PowerShell script that runs the steps in order.

Download the toolkit (ct-migration.zip)

FileRuns onPurpose
ctmig.ps1VMOrchestrator: Precheck, Init, InstallJob, Sync, Status, Validate, ReloadTable, Cutover, Rollback, Cleanup
config.psd1-Server names, logins, options
sql/01_source_enable_ct.sqlAzureCT on the database and every PK table
sql/02_target_linked_server.sqlVMLinked server from the VM to Azure SQL Database
sql/03_target_framework.sqlVMsync schema: control tables and generic procedures
sql/04_target_agent_job.sqlVMAgent job running the delta sync every N minutes
sql/90_source_set_mode.sqlAzureREAD_ONLY for cutover, READ_WRITE for rollback
sql/98_…, sql/99_…bothCleanup

Configure

Everything environment-specific lives in config.psd1. Passwords are never stored. They come from CTMIG_SRC_PWD / CTMIG_TGT_PWD or a prompt.

  • InitialLoad = 'Dacpac': schema and data in one DACPAC, which is fine for 2.3 GB. For bigger databases, 'LinkedServer' publishes the schema only and copies each table over the link.
  • RetentionDays must be longer than the whole migration window. If CT history is cleaned up before you sync it, that table has to be reloaded.
  • LinkUser is the Azure login the linked server uses. When it's the same as SourceUser, the password is reused.

The linked server needs the Microsoft OLE DB Driver on the VM. Check which providers you have:

EXEC master.sys.sp_enum_oledb_providers;   -- look for MSOLEDBSQL / MSOLEDBSQL19

Either works against Azure SQL Database. Driver 19 encrypts by default, which can break linked servers to on-premises servers with self-signed certificates, but Azure always encrypts and has a trusted certificate.

Precheck

cd B:\ct-migration
.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Precheck

Read the output, not just the colours:

  • tables_without_pk = 0. Every table can use CT. Tables without a PK would be copied in full during the cutover window, which adds downtime.
  • updateability = READ_ONLY. This was left over from Lab 6, where Azure was frozen before bcp out. CT is enabled with an ALTER DATABASE, so the source must be writable. Fix it from master:
-- on cisql01, connected to master
ALTER DATABASE [scsbank] SET READ_WRITE;
  • Agent: Running, which the scheduled sync needs, and is_sysadmin = 1, which the linked server and sp_configure need.

Init: CT, baseline, DACPAC, linked server, first sync

.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Init          # add -Force only if the target database exists AND is empty

Init runs nine steps. Here they are with this lab's output.

1Enable CT  2Baseline  3Extract

What step 1 runs on Azure, for the database and then for every table with a PK:

ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON (CHANGE_RETENTION = 7 DAYS, AUTO_CLEANUP = ON);
ALTER TABLE [Account].[Account] ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING WITH (TRACK_COLUMNS_UPDATED = OFF);
-- ...generated for all 17 tables

The baseline is 0 because nothing had been committed since CT was switched on. It's saved to B:\ctmig\work\baseline_version.txt.

4Publish to the VM

Same publish switches as Lab 6: AllowIncompatiblePlatform, because the DACPAC is stamped for Azure, and ExcludeObjectTypes=Users;Logins;RoleMembership;Permissions, because Azure contained users don't map to a VM. The publish with 16.7 million rows took 8 min 28 s. The application is still running the whole time.

5Linked server  6Framework  7Register  8Prepare  9First sync

  • "remote query timeout (s) changed from 600 to 0. Run the RECONFIGURE statement to install." is not an error. sp_configure always prints it, and the script runs RECONFIGURE on the next line. The 600-second default would kill any long reload over the link.
  • scsbank | 0 | 5 is the linked server smoke test: remote database, CT version, and engine edition 5 = Azure SQL Database.
  • CT | 17 | 0: 17 tables in CT mode, none missing a baseline.
  • FK | 25 | 25: 25 foreign keys switched to NOCHECK. Deltas arrive table by table, so a child row can briefly arrive before its parent. Their original state is saved and restored WITH CHECK at cutover. Triggers would be disabled the same way, so replayed changes don't fire business logic twice.

The linked server it creates, condensed:

EXEC sp_addlinkedserver @server = N'AZSQL', @srvproduct = N'', @provider = N'MSOLEDBSQL',
     @datasrc = N'cisql01.database.windows.net', @catalog = N'scsbank';   -- catalog is required for Azure
EXEC sp_addlinkedsrvlogin @rmtsrvname = N'AZSQL', @useself = 'false', @rmtuser = N'nsunke', @rmtpassword = N'…';
EXEC sp_serveroption N'AZSQL', 'rpc out', 'true';
EXEC sp_serveroption N'AZSQL', 'remote proc transaction promotion', 'false';   -- no MSDTC
EXEC sp_configure 'remote query timeout (s)', 0;  RECONFIGURE;

What one delta sync actually does

There's no hand-written code per table. sync.usp_sync_table reads the target's metadata (sys.columns, the PK columns, sys.dm_exec_describe_first_result_set) and builds the statements on the fly. For one table, a run does this:

-- 1. new watermark, read BEFORE pulling (overlap is safe, gaps are not)
SELECT CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION(), CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION(OBJECT_ID('[Account].[Account]'));
--    last_version < min_valid  →  error 50001: history gone, reload the table

-- 2. pull net changes + current values through the linked server (one statement = consistent under RCSI)
INSERT stg.[Account__Account]
EXEC ('SELECT ct.SYS_CHANGE_OPERATION, ct.AccountID AS __ct_AccountID,
              CASE WHEN t.AccountID IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS __exists, t.*
       FROM CHANGETABLE(CHANGES Account.Account, @last) ct
       LEFT JOIN Account.Account t ON t.AccountID = ct.AccountID') AT AZSQL;

-- 3. apply, in one transaction together with the watermark
MERGE Account.Account AS t
USING stg.[Account__Account] AS s ON t.AccountID = s.__ct_AccountID
WHEN MATCHED AND s.__exists = 0 THEN DELETE                -- gone at the source
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET …                             -- latest values win
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET AND s.__exists = 1 THEN INSERT …;
UPDATE sync.control SET last_version = @new_version WHERE …;

(This is simplified. The real generated statements list every column, add IDENTITY_INSERT where needed, and cast types that can't travel over a linked server, such as geography/hierarchyid as varbinary(max) and xml/json as nvarchar(max).)

  • Deletes are detected by "the row no longer exists at the source", not by trusting the D flag. That one rule also covers a row inserted and then deleted, and a primary-key update, which CT reports as delete-old plus insert-new.
  • The watermark moves in the same transaction as the MERGE. If a run fails, nothing moves and the next run retries.
  • The staging table is rebuilt every run, so a column added to the target with a schema-only DACPAC publish is picked up automatically.
  • Computed columns, rowversion and GENERATED ALWAYS columns are skipped. The target generates its own values.

Schedule the sync and watch it

.\ctmig.ps1 -Step InstallJob
.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Status

An application lock inside sync.usp_sync_all stops a manual sync and the Agent job from overlapping. Tables run parents-first, in foreign-key depth order. Everything is logged in sync.log.

The source here is serverless. A query every 15 minutes keeps it from auto-pausing for the whole migration window, so you pay for that compute. Plan the sync window and don't leave the job running for weeks.

Validate while the source is live

.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Validate

For every table it compares COUNT_BIG(*) and CHECKSUM_AGG(BINARY_CHECKSUM(…)) on Azure (through the linked server) and on the VM.

Then more transactions arrived on Azure, and I validated again before the next sync:

That's the point of this screenshot: Txn.AccountTransaction has 7,500,420 rows on Azure and 7,500,369 on the VM. Account.Beneficiary has the same row count but a different checksum, meaning rows were updated, not inserted. After the sync job ran:

Mismatches while the source is writable just mean "changes since the last sync". The validation that counts is the one after the source is frozen, and the cutover step enforces it.

Cutover

.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Cutover
TimeStepWhat happened
17:11:18ConfirmType CUTOVER, so nobody runs it by accident
17:11:391. Catch-up syncSource still writable; makes the final delta tiny
17:12:00Stop the appThe script waits for Enter. Downtime starts here
17:12:042. Source READ_ONLYALTER DATABASE [scsbank] SET READ_ONLY WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE from master
17:12:043. Disable jobNothing else touches the target
17:12:074. Final sync17 / 0 in 3 seconds
17:13:025. Validation17 / 17 OK. Any mismatch stops here with the source still read-only
17:13:396. FinalizeFKs WITH CHECK (trusted again), triggers, identity reseed, sequences

The application was down for about 1 min 40 s, and nearly all of that was verification: the checksum over 16.76 million rows and re-validating 25 foreign keys. Moving the data itself took 3 seconds. Compare that with Lab 6, where the application was down for the whole bcp out + bcp in.

Finalize only reported FOREIGN KEY | OK | 25. This schema has no identity columns or sequences to realign, so those checks had nothing to report. On a schema that has them, the target's identity is reseeded so it's never behind Azure, and each sequence restarts after Azure's current value.

Rollback

Until the application is pointed at the VM, the source is untouched apart from being read-only. Going back is one command:

.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Rollback     # source READ_WRITE, target re-prepared, sync job re-enabled

After cutover

  • Logins and users: they weren't migrated (excluded from the publish). Create logins on the VM and map database users with ALTER USER … WITH LOGIN = ….
  • Repoint the application connection string to MSSQLSRV01.
  • Instance-level objects the app relies on, such as Agent jobs, linked servers and Database Mail, have to be recreated.
  • TDE: like Lab 5, the target isn't encrypted. Enable it afterwards with the same certificate steps (the database is live, so it's a background scan).
  • Clean up when you're satisfied:
.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Cleanup                    # Agent job, sync/stg schemas, linked server
.\ctmig.ps1 -Step Cleanup -DisableSourceCT   # also CT off on Azure (skipped while it is READ_ONLY)

02_target_linked_server.sql set remote query timeout to 0 server-wide. Put it back to 600 if your standards require it.

Will it work with any SQL Server database?

The engine (Change Tracking + generated MERGE) is generic and works for any schema that meets the conditions below. The orchestration around it (ctmig.ps1, the linked server, the Agent job) was built and tested for one route: Azure SQL Database → SQL Server on a VM.

Source and target combinations

Source → TargetWorks?Why / what changes
Azure SQL Database → SQL Server VMYes, tested in this labWhat the toolkit was built for
SQL Server (on-prem/VM) → SQL Server VMWith small changesSQL authentication only (see below). Source on SQL Server 2017+, because 01_source_enable_ct.sql uses STRING_AGG. For SQL Server → SQL Server, log shipping, an availability group or backup/restore are usually simpler anyway.
Any SQL Server → Azure SQL DatabaseNoThe engine runs on the target and needs a linked server, SQL Agent and sp_configure, and Azure SQL Database has none of them. Use transactional replication instead (Lab 4).
Target older than SQL Server 2017NoThe framework uses STRING_AGG and CREATE OR ALTER

Schema requirements on the source

Table typeWhat happens
Has a primary keySynced with CT + MERGE
No primary keyCT can't track it, so it gets a full copy during cutover, which adds downtime. Add a PK first if you can.
Composite PK, identity, foreign keys, triggers, sequencesHandled
geography, geometry, hierarchyid, xml, json, vectorConverted to a type the linked server can carry, then converted back on the target
Computed, rowversionSkipped; the target generates them
System-versioned temporal tablesNot handled. The history table gets registered like a normal table, but you can't MERGE into it while versioning is on. Turn SYSTEM_VERSIONING off on the target during the sync, or exclude the history table.
Memory-optimized tablesNot supported. Change Tracking can't be enabled on them.
Ledger tables, graph (node/edge) tablesNot supported
Sparse columns with a column setNot handled: SELECT * returns the column set instead of the individual columns

Two things force a table to be reloaded (fully copied again): a TRUNCATE or partition switch on the source, and CT retention running out before the next sync. Both raise error 50001, and -AutoReload or -Step ReloadTable fixes them, but for a very large table that's a long copy.

On scale: each table's delta is applied as one transaction. A burst of changes, such as a mass update of millions of rows, means a big MERGE and target log growth. Syncing more often keeps each delta small.

On-prem SQL Server as the source: SQL authentication, not Windows

Source connections use SQL authentication only: ctmig.ps1 connects with -U SourceUser, SqlPackage passes /SourceUser and /SourcePassword, and the linked server maps to a SQL login (@useself = 'false'). The target can use either (TargetAuth = 'SQL' or 'Windows').

Windows authentication for the source would need more than a config switch. sqlcmd and SqlPackage could use integrated security easily. The linked server is the problem: a Windows login passing through the VM to another server is a Kerberos double hop. It fails unless SPNs and delegation are configured, and especially when the Agent job runs under a service account. SQL authentication avoids all of that.

Even with SQL authentication, check these on an on-prem source:

RequirementWhyCheck / fix
Mixed Mode authenticationMany on-prem servers allow Windows logins onlySELECT SERVERPROPERTY('IsIntegratedSecurityOnly') must return 0
Default instance on port 1433The script connects to tcp:<server>,1433Named instances and other ports need a script change
Trusted TLS certificate on the sourceODBC Driver 18 (sqlcmd) and SqlPackage encrypt by default and reject self-signed certificates, which most on-prem servers useGive the source a certificate from your CA, or add a source trust-certificate option to the script (today it exists for the target only)
Linked server providerMSOLEDBSQL19 encrypts by default and fails on a self-signed certificate. MSOLEDBSQL (v18) doesn't.Provider = 'MSOLEDBSQL'
SQL Server 2017+ on the sourceSTRING_AGG in the CT enable scriptSELECT @@VERSION
RCSI on the source (recommended)Azure SQL Database has it by default. Without it, the delta reads take shared locks and can block the application.ALTER DATABASE … SET READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON
Login rightsdb_owner to enable CT; sysadmin (or ALTER ANY DATABASE) to set READ_ONLY at cutoverSame as with Azure
Before pointing the toolkit at a new database, run -Step Precheck against it. Look for tables without a PK, temporal or memory-optimized tables, and the SQL Server version, before you commit to a cutover date.

Troubleshooting (what I actually hit)

ProblemCauseFix
Precheck: Named Pipes Provider: Could not open a connection to SQL Server [53]Typo in TargetServer (mssqlsrv0). Error 53 means the name wasn't found at all, so it never got as far as a login failureUse the exact name from SELECT @@SERVERNAME, or localhost when running on the VM
Init step 1: Msg 5004 … must be in a writable state, Msg 3906 … database is read-onlySource still frozen from Lab 6ALTER DATABASE [scsbank] SET READ_WRITE from master. If it's a geo-replication secondary, point at the primary
Init: Target database 'scsbank' already existsInit publishes into a new databaseDrop it, or -Force if it's empty. The script now counts rows and refuses if there's any data
Configuration option 'remote query timeout (s)' changed … Run the RECONFIGURE statementInformational sp_configure messageNothing. The script runs RECONFIGURE on the next line
Sync: error 50001 CT history no longer validRetention expired, TRUNCATE or a partition switch on the source-Step Sync -AutoReload or -Step ReloadTable -Table schema.table
Validate shows ROW_MISMATCH before cutoverChanges since the last syncExpected. Sync, then validate again
Linked server: SSL / certificate chain not trustedA TLS-inspecting proxy or firewall between the VM and AzureNot a driver problem. Fix the path or the certificate store

Lab 5 vs Lab 6 vs Lab 7

Lab 5: BACPACLab 6: DACPAC + BCPLab 7: DACPAC + CT
Application down duringExport + importbcp out + bcp inFinal delta + validation only (~1 min 40 s here)
Grows with database size?YesYesOnly the validation part; the final sync depends on how much changed
Moving parts2 commandsPer-table scriptsCT, linked server, Agent job (scripted)
RollbackRestart on AzureRestart on AzureOne command, any time before repointing
Rehearse before the real dayFull rerunFull rerunRun Validate as often as you like while live
Changes to the sourceNoneNoneCT enabled (small overhead), turned off afterwards
TDE on targetAfter import (scan)Before loadAfter cutover (scan)

For production-sized databases with many tables, a CDC-based tool such as Oracle GoldenGate for SQL Server does the same job continuously, with near-zero downtime. Azure Data Factory with the same Change Tracking pattern is the Azure-native alternative. For a lab, or a few hundred tables, the native Change Tracking engine here goes a long way with nothing extra to license.
